preconditions.description: The number of packets n is between 1 and 10 inclusive.
The list a contains exactly n integers.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= 1000 for x in a)
preconditions.description: Each packet contains between 1 and 1000 balloons inclusive.

postconditions.expression: (n == 1 or sum(a) % 2 == 0 and all(x == a[0] for x in a)) == (stdout.strip() == '-1')
postconditions.description: Output is -1 if and only if it is impossible to satisfy the conditions (n=1, or n>1 but all packets are equal leading to equal sums for any split).

postconditions.expression: (n > 1 and not all(x == a[0] for x in a)) == (stdout.strip() != '-1')
postconditions.description: Output is a valid assignment if and only if n > 1 and not all packet sizes are identical.
If a solution exists, the output starts with an integer k representing the count of packets for Grigory.
If a solution exists, the number of indices following k matches k exactly.

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() != '-1') == (all(1 <= int(idx) <= n for idx in stdout.strip().split()[1:]))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, all provided indices are valid 1-based packet indices.
If a solution exists, all provided indices are distinct.
If a solution exists, Grigory receives at least one packet and at least one packet remains for Andrew.

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() != '-1') == (sum(a[int(idx)-1] for idx in stdout.strip().split()[1:]) != sum(a) - sum(a[int(idx)-1] for idx in stdout.strip().split()[1:]))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the sum of balloons in Grigory's packets is not equal to the sum of balloons in Andrew's packets.
